links.outcome: Accuracy of residents' ChatGPT responses on a clinical topic and self-rated AI proficiency
links.effect: Low AI proficiency among residents; only 21% accurate responses with third-party questioning due to misinterpreted medical acronyms; most residents dissatisfied with their AI training.
links.quote: Interaction with ChatGPT regarding clinical signs of acute hepatic steatosis gravidarum revealed a preference for third-party questioning, resulting in only 21% accurate responses due to misinterpretation of medical acronyms.

links.outcome: Relationship between self-assessed AI skills and accuracy of ChatGPT responses
links.effect: No correlation between AI response accuracy and self-assessed IT or AI skills; most residents dissatisfied with AI training; perceived versus actual AI proficiency discrepancy.
links.quote: No correlation was found between AI response accuracy and the residents' self-assessed IT or AI skills, with most expressing dissatisfaction with their AI training.

unlisted_practices: Structured AI literacy and prompt-engineering training in medical education

screen.reason: Evaluates obstetrics residents' interaction styles and accuracy when querying ChatGPT on clinical scenarios, observing how prompt styles impact accuracy without testing an organizational deployment safeguard intervention.
